institutions: West Virginia State Capitol Complex — seat of state government; the Cass Gilbert-designed capitol was dedicated June 20, 1932 and the complex occupies 16 acres along the Kanawha River.
CAMC (Vandalia Health) — nonprofit 1,138-bed regional referral center of seven hospitals, and West Virginia's principal medical teaching facility.
West Virginia State University, Institute — public land-grant HBCU founded in 1891; roughly 3,500 students and more than 70 undergraduate and graduate programs.
University of Charleston — private university at 2300 MacCorkle Ave SE, on the Kanawha riverfront directly across from the capitol complex.
WVU Medicine Thomas Memorial Hospital — acute-care hospital in South Charleston with a 24-hour emergency room and graduate medical education programs.
highlights: The West Virginia State Capitol is one of the few state capitols with a gold-leafed dome, rising 293 feet — five feet higher than the dome of the U.S. Capitol.

East End Historic District — one of nine Charleston districts on the National Register of Historic Places, and the only one subject to city design review; Elk City Historic District on the West Side is another.

Clay Center for the Arts & Sciences — 240,000-square-foot downtown venue opened in 2003, housing the Juliet Art Museum, Avampato Discovery Museum, Caperton Planetarium and Maier Foundation Performance Hall.
Kanawha State Forest — 9,300 acres with more than 60 miles of hiking and biking trails, seven miles from downtown Charleston.
